mission: Make it dramatically easier for an ordinary human with a meaningful vision to accomplish extraordinary things with AI without becoming an AI project manager.
human_intent: Reconcile the AppDeploy target with the actual canonical React Hub, preserve the existing architecture, verify the runtime, and make the resulting lesson improve the machine-readable system.
naya_understanding: The AppDeploy target is a ready static source mirror, while the canonical GitHub Hub is a multi-file React/Vite application. The current AppDeploy snapshot does not contain the canonical React source tree, and the available AppDeploy deployment surface has no repository-import/build-from-GitHub operation. Therefore silently replacing the mirror with a hand-recreated React approximation would violate the no-competing-system and preserve-architecture constraints.

authority.human_authorization: Explicit continuation baton in current execution context

constraints: Do not create a competing React renderer.
Do not rebuild SmartFeedBoard from scratch when the canonical component already exists.
Do not claim browser or runtime proof without actual browser evidence.
Do not treat AppDeploy READY as React-source equivalence.
Do not downgrade the canonical React Hub to a static approximation.
Leave exactly one executable successor action.
plan: Inventory canonical React Hub source and existing AppDeploy snapshot.
Determine the smallest safe deployment path using existing architecture.
Attempt runtime reconciliation only when the available deployment surface can preserve the architecture.
Record the first material boundary and convert it into machine-readable system memory.

actions.result: Current canonical React Hub source observed at commit 7dd17a81f5d2c58aa8e0fc37b2a92131b51c1df8.
Canonical React architecture includes App.tsx, AppShellV3, routes, identity/session, AuthPanel, PIS, SmartFeedBoard, cognition, types, and a dedicated multi-file style system.
Applied snapshot contains a static loader with package.json, index.html, src/main.ts, src/styles.css and no canonical React source tree.
READY with empty frontend/backend error arrays; this proves deployment health only, not React equivalence or browser behavior.

observations: Canonical React source is materially larger than the AppDeploy mirror snapshot.
The AppDeploy utility surface available in this execution does not expose a repository-import or GitHub-source build operation.
Hand-recreating only the visible shell would create a second implementation and lose existing SmartFeedBoard/PIS/identity architecture.

The correct next engineering move is to establish a canonical React build artifact handoff into the existing AppDeploy application, then deploy that artifact without changing the product architecture.
result: The requested reconciliation was inspected to the architecture boundary. The existing AppDeploy application cannot safely become the canonical React Hub through the currently exposed deployment operation without transferring the full canonical React source/build artifact. No competing approximation was deployed. The AppDeploy target remains ready as the prior static mirror.

value_cost_risk.value: Prevents an apparently successful deployment from silently replacing the canonical React product with an incomplete imitation.
value_cost_risk.cost: Architecture inventory and runtime capability inspection.
value_cost_risk.risk: The AppDeploy target remains the static mirror until a canonical React build artifact can be transferred and deployed.

lesson: A deployment surface is only a valid canonical runtime lane if it can preserve and build the actual canonical source architecture. When the runtime surface cannot ingest that architecture, the correct repair is to create a verified source/build handoff—not to recreate the UI approximately.
memory: AppDeploy READY does not imply canonical React equivalence.
The canonical Hub is a React/Vite source tree, not the recovered static HTML mirror.
The canonical SmartFeedBoard, AppShellV3, PIS, identity, routes, and style system must remain the implementation source.
A future AppDeploy deployment must bind to an exact React build artifact produced from the canonical GitHub commit.
Browser acceptance remains a separate evidence boundary.

next_action.instruction: Establish the canonical React build-artifact handoff from GitHub main into the existing AppDeploy application, bind the artifact to an exact source commit, deploy it without recreating the architecture, then verify desktop/mobile/interaction and record the runtime evidence.
